html:
E. V. Ramasamy, known as Periyar, "the great one", was the founder of the Dravidian movement in south India. For fifty years he attacked caste, the rule of Brahmins and religion itself, and Tamil politics still runs on lines he drew.

He was born in 1879 at Erode, the son of a rich merchant, and left school at ten. He joined the Congress in 1919 and led the Vaikom Satyagraha in 1924 for the right of the lowest castes to walk on roads near a temple. He left Congress in 1925, saying it was run by and for Brahmins.

That year he began the Self-Respect Movement. Its teaching:

  • caste is a fraud, and the Hindu texts that defend it should be burnt;
  • there is no god; he led processions that smashed idols;
  • marriages need no priest; women should choose their husbands, own property, divorce and remarry.

He also held that the Tamils and other southerners were Dravidians, a people distinct from the north. In 1937 he led protests against making Hindi a school subject, and later asked for a separate southern state.

His follower C. N. Annadurai left in 1949 to form a party, which won power in Tamil Nadu in 1967. No national party has governed the state since.
